name: Koshun
description: 'Fragrance of Shizuoka'. A remarkable modern cultivar bred specifically for its astonishingly powerful and unique floral aroma. It produces a Sencha with a perfume-like fragrance reminiscent of lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, and cherry leaves, offering a completely different experience from classic, umami-focused Japanese green teas.
plantType: Upright, vigorous bush with long, elegant leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Well-suited to the climate of Shizuoka, where it was developed.
processing: Processing Koshun is all about capturing its volatile aromatic compounds. It is typically lightly steamed (Asamushi) to prevent the heat from damaging the delicate floral notes. Careful, low-temperature drying is also crucial.
oxidation: Zero oxidation for the Sencha style. The leaves are steamed immediately to lock in the floral aroma.
roasting: A very gentle, low-temperature final drying roast is used to avoid baking away the prized floral fragrance.
versatility: Moderately versatile. While its primary use is for a unique style of aromatic Sencha, its genetics also make it suitable for crafting fragrant Japanese oolongs.

Sencha.Aromatic Sencha: Its primary expression. A lightly steamed green tea where processing is entirely focused on preserving its unique, intense floral bouquet.

Japanese Oolong.Light Oolong: Its aromatic potential also makes it a great candidate for producing lightly oxidized Japanese oolongs.

sensory.aroma: Intense lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, cherry leaf, very perfume-like
sensory.flavor: Light-bodied, highly aromatic, with a sweet, floral taste and a clean, fragrant finish.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Smooth and light with very low astringency. The liquor is a very pale, bright green-yellow.
